messages:
zara (Support): hey team — escalation from Acme Corp. They report a sudden p95/p99 latency regression on calls that use function/tool-calling + structured JSON output. Started ~4h ago after a deploy. customer says normal text completions are fine but any request with tools/schema validation jumps by ~300-800ms at p95 and up to +1.2s at p99. request_id: acme-req-20260215-42. can we triage? :warning:

Ethan (SRE): thanks zara. can you paste a repro payload and the model + region + any logs you have? also did they switch models or config recently?

zara (Support): pasted repro below. model: rdx-large-2026 (hosted-us-west). region: us-west-2. customer says they didn't change their prompts; we rolled runtime v2.14.1 ~5h ago. logs from our tracing show two hotspots: `tool-router` RPC and `json-validator` step. snippet from trace (timings are ms):
```
trace: acme-req-20260215-42
- request.receive: 12
- auth.check: 3
- route.selection: 8
- tool-router.call: 120  <-- increased
- runtime.invoke: 15
- json-validator.validate: 310  <-- big spike
- response.serialize: 5
- total: 483
```

zara (Support): repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model":"rdx-large-2026",
    "input":"Summarize and call tools",
    "tools": ["lookup_customer","format_invoice"],
    "output_schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"invoice_html":{"type":"string"}},"required":["invoice_html"]}
  }'
```

Maya (Client Success): customer notes spike only when `output_schema` present or when they use tool-router -> so two orthogonal things. they can repro consistently. They asked for a mitigation ASAP because their UI times out at 700ms.

Ethan (SRE): first-pass hypotheses: 1) schema validation is running synchronously in the request path and doing JSON-schema compile/validate each request, 2) tool-router RPC path added an extra network hop (TLS + deserialize) after the runtime change, 3) increased model latency can amplify validation time (longer tokens => more bytes to validate).

Alex (Infra): I pulled the service traces. After the last runtime deploy we added a synchronous schema validator call in the inference worker to ensure strict structured output for a rollout. It looks like we forgot to enable the schema compile-cache and we also run the validator on the hot path instead of a worker pool. two quick data points:
- validator cold-compile time: ~200-350ms for that schema (regexes + ajv-style lib),
- subsequent validates (same process) drop to ~4-12ms when compiled.

Alex (Infra): tool-router: we started shipping a tiny RPC wrapper that pulls tool definitions from the catalog on first use; for the customer the wrapper is doing a RPC to the 'catalog-service' to fetch metadata because they use a dynamic tool-set. that RPC costs ~100-140ms (TLS + cert validation + auth). we had expected catalog to be cached but for dynamic workspaces it misses on first requests.

Ethan (SRE): good find. that matches trace. mitigations we can try immediately: 1) enable schema compile-cache in the runtime (config flag) so first-compile is cached across workers, 2) offload schema validation to the validation threadpool (async) and return results prior to finalizing tokens—if validation fails, we can degrade to a soft warning or fallback, 3) warm the tool-router/cached catalog for that workspace (pre-warm call) and add a temporary caching layer on client side for the customer.

zara (Support): can we do any fast feature-flag/patch we can flip for Acme while we work on the long-term fix? their SLA request is urgent.

Alex (Infra): yes — we can flip two things per-workspace: `validate_schema=false` and `catalog_cache_ttl=1h` as a temporary mitigation. I've deployed a per-tenant flag toggle UI; can flip now for acme workspace id acme-42. if we flip `validate_schema=false` their p95 drops in our staging to ~180ms for the same payload (from ~480). measured on the same model/infra.

Maya (Client Success): please flip and I'll confirm with the customer. also we should note this as a known regression in the support KB.

Ethan (SRE): follow-up longer-term engineering work:
- instrument per-component compile times in the Console traces (AJV compile + validate counters),
- add compiled schema cache shared across inference workers (LRU with eviction),
- move validation off the hot path into validation thread pool or async task + allow a behavioral fallback (soft/strict modes),
- change tool-router to use persistent mTLS connections with connection pooling to catalog-service and pre-warm fetches for dynamic tool lists,
- add sampling of full traces at 5% and create alert if per-tenant schema compile time > 150ms for 3/5 samples.

Ethan (SRE): short repro steps for infra/eng teams to validate locally:
1) checkout runtime branch: `git checkout release/v2.14.1-hotfix`
2) build docker image: `make docker-build RUNTIME=runtime:v2.14.1-hotfix`
3) run local compose (includes catalog-service): `docker-compose -f docker/local.yaml up --build`
4) send curl payload (same as above) with workspace header `X-Workspace: acme-42`
5) observe `validator.compile` span in the trace (zipkin/opentelemetry) and the `tool-router` RPC spans

zara (Support): Alex — went ahead and flipped `validate_schema=false` and `catalog_cache_ttl=3600` for acme-42. Maya — customer reported UI no longer times out, p95 ~190ms. they accepted temporary workaround.

Maya (Client Success): they want ETA for permanent fix and a postmortem. they are fine with the flag for now but want timeline.

Alex (Infra): ETA for low-effort permanent fix (cache + threadpool): 2-3 sprints to implement + QA. we can prioritize and do an accelerated patch in 1 sprint if we reassign a pair. I'll schedule time. PRs: add schema-cache (shared LRU), move validator to threadpool + metric emit.

Ethan (SRE): I'll open an incident-ticket and link traces + initial mitigation here. action owners: Alex (infra) for infra patch, Ethan (SRE) for tracing/alerts, Maya (Client Success) to communicate timeline, zara to coordinate with customer.

DevBot: incident created -> INC-2026-042, priority P2, owner: Ethan (SRE).

zara (Support): thanks all — leaving notes in the customer ticket and KB. will follow up when dev PRs land. :thumbsup:
